headlines.summary: 국민의힘 소득세법 일부 개정안 발의 주식·디지털자산 간 형평성 논란 확산 해외·DEX 등 과세 사각지대 발생 우려 재경부 “소득에 과세 원칙…논란 파악” 내년부터 개인투자자의 디지털자산 양도차익에 과세가 시행되는 가운데 야당이 이를 폐지하는 법안을 추진한다. 금융투자소득세가 폐지된 상황에서 주식과 디지털자산 간 과세 체계 형평성에 문제가 있다는 이유에서다.

top5_headlines.summary: 핵심요약 KDI 김민호 선임연구위원, 'KDI 보고서' 발표 창업 이후 업력 8~19년 기업, 성장 정체 심화 생산성·인력·시장 병목 진단 후 맞춤 지원 필요 KDI 김민호 선임연구위원. KDI 제공 기업 성장 둔화가 심화하는 가운데, 정부의 기업 지원 방식이 '맞춤형 원스톱 체계'로 전환돼야 한다는 제언이 나왔다.

key_headlines.title: Vice Premier Koo Yoon-cheol: Oil Price Adjustments Inevitable, Fuel Tax Cuts to Mitigate Burden
key_headlines.summary: Vice Premier Koo Yoon-cheol stated that adjusting the maximum oil price system would lead to inevitable price increases, which will be counteracted by fuel tax cuts to minimize public burden. He also announced a 'war supplementary budget' to be submitted this month and discussed expanding policy financing to 20 trillion won.

key_headlines.title: President Lee Jae-myung Activates Middle East War Emergency Response System, Vows Crackdown on Oil Price Collusion
key_headlines.summary: President Lee Jae-myung emphasized the activation of an emergency response system to the Middle East conflict during a cabinet meeting, reiterating the need for swift processing of a 'war supplementary budget.' He also pledged to severely punish any collusion in oil prices.

key_headlines.title: Government Mandates 5-Day Vehicle Rotation for Public Sector, Encourages Voluntary Participation for Private Sector
key_headlines.summary: To conserve energy, the government is mandating a 5-day vehicle rotation system for 1.5 million public sector employees, with repeated violations subject to disciplinary action. Private companies are encouraged to participate voluntarily, aiming to save 3,000 barrels of oil daily.

key_headlines.title: Vice Premier Koo Yoon-cheol Highlights Soaring Diesel Prices, Reaffirms Fuel Tax Cuts for Public Relief
key_headlines.summary: Vice Premier Koo Yoon-cheol pointed out the particularly high surge in diesel prices and reiterated the government's commitment to minimize the public's burden through fuel tax cuts. This was discussed during a cabinet meeting chaired by President Lee Jae-myung, addressing the high oil prices and exchange rate volatility due to Middle East variables.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's Effective Property Tax Rate Half of OECD Average, But GDP Burden is Average
key_headlines.summary: A report indicates that South Korea's effective property tax rate is around 0.15%, which is half the OECD average, partly due to the previous administration's tax burden reduction measures. However, the burden of property tax relative to GDP is consistent with the OECD average.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea is actively responding to the economic fallout from the Middle East conflict, with Vice Premier Koo Yoon-cheol discussing a 'war supplementary budget' and fuel tax cuts to stabilize prices and support livelihoods. President Lee Jae-myung has activated an emergency response system, vowing strict action against oil price collusion. The government is also pushing for energy conservation measures, including a mandatory 5-day vehicle rotation system for the public sector, and promoting energy-saving practices among the public.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The impending appointment of Shin Hyun-song as the new Bank of Korea Governor is drawing attention, particularly his stance on monetary policy amidst growing inflation concerns due to the Middle East situation. Producer prices have continued their upward trend for six consecutive months, driven by financial services and petroleum products, with a 0.6% monthly increase and a 2.4% year-on-year rise in February. There are warnings that a prolonged Middle East crisis could jeopardize the 2% economic growth forecast, potentially pushing it down to the 1% range, making a 25 trillion won 'war supplementary budget' a potential breakthrough.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market initially experienced a sharp decline, with the KOSPI falling over 6% due to a 'triple whammy' of rising oil prices, a weak won, and fears of US interest rate hikes, leading to record individual buying and triggering a market-wide circuit breaker. However, subsequent trading saw the KOSPI and KOSDAQ rebound by about 2%, spurred by hopes of US-Iran negotiations, though gains were reduced from intraday highs. Amidst this volatility and the won-dollar exchange rate breaching 1,510, investors are increasingly turning to dollar-parking ETFs as a safe haven.
sections.Industry & Technology: POSCO Group Chairman Jang In-hwa announced that the company aims to realize 'two-core' business performance in steel and battery materials this year, focusing on securing profitability from joint ventures and initiating commercial production of lithium. Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST) developed 'virtual battery' technology to integrate multiple electric vehicles into the power grid, accelerating the commercialization of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) systems. The government also plans to expand nuclear and coal power generation to address LNG supply instability and launched an energy-saving campaign, encouraging practices like charging electric vehicles during off-peak hours.
sections.Real Estate: The Korea Land and Housing Corporation (LH) is actively recruiting residents for 9,120 leasehold homes for specific demographics including newlyweds, new parents, and multi-child families, with applications open until the end of the year. In a significant urban development, HanmiGlobal has secured a contract to support the architect selection for the massive Olympic Village reconstruction project in Songpa-gu, set to create 9,218 new units. The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport emphasized the government's commitment to expanding housing supply and improving financial soundness, particularly addressing issues like Jeonse fraud, as new heads were appointed to key real estate agencies.
sections.International Economy: Despite public pronouncements, European nations are reportedly offering crucial military support to the U.S. for operations in the Middle East, contradicting former President Trump's criticisms. U.S. Federal Reserve officials are divided on the necessity of interest rate hikes in response to inflation and rising oil prices, with some advocating for increases if inflation persists, while others caution against premature action. Trump's statements regarding the Middle East conflict and potential agreements continue to induce market volatility, causing fluctuations in oil prices and a decline in gold values.
sections.AI & Economy: Maeil Business Newspaper is celebrating its 60th anniversary by positioning itself as a leader in AI innovation, aiming to integrate AI technology with its extensive news and data assets to provide enhanced economic insights and investment information. The government is committed to supporting AI companies' global expansion through incentives and export programs, while also adopting AI agents in internal procurement processes. Kakao is significantly advancing its AI monetization strategy by expanding its 'ChatGPT for Kakao' service to include shopping partners like Olive Young and Musinsa, allowing users to interact with AI agents for purchases. Furthermore, Gwangju's Advanced 3rd District is embarking on a strategic plan to become a national AI capital, developing a comprehensive complex for AI industry, research, and residential living. The need for a 'Space Cloud Korea Team' strategy is highlighted to integrate AI semiconductors, cloud software, and services for competitive AI infrastructure.
sections.Others: Reports from US media about negotiations between the US and Iran's Parliament Speaker to end the war were strongly denied by the Speaker himself, despite former President Trump's claims of an agreement. Experts warn that even if the Iran war concludes, the global economy could face a severe 'high oil price aftershock,' potentially leading to stagflation. Larry Fink, CEO of BlackRock, cautioned that the AI boom risks exacerbating wealth inequality by disproportionately benefiting the wealthy, urging for broader distribution of AI's advantages. Meanwhile, US LNG exporters are emerging as significant beneficiaries of the Iran war due to surging demand, impacting energy-importing nations like South Korea.
